rulebook: Manual of Policies and Procedures, Community Care Licensing Division: Child Care Center General Licensing Requirements, Title 22, Division 12, Chapter 1 (Subchapter 1 general requirements; Subchapter 2 infant care centers; Subchapter 3 school-age child care centers; Subchapter 4 centers for mildly ill children), current through Manual Letter No. CCL-23-13 (eff. 10/1/23)

findings.requirement: Each licensee must have and keep on file a current written plan of operation, including admission policies, staffing, menus, transportation, and rates.
findings.quote: Each licensee shall have and keep on file a current written, definitive plan of operation.
findings.handbook_quote: Our written plan of operation, which describes our program goals, admission policies, staffing, sample menus, transportation, and rates, is kept on file here, and you may read it at the front desk.

findings.requirement: The plan of operation must include a rate-setting policy, including a policy on refunds.
findings.quote: Rate-setting policy including, but not limited to, a policy on refunds.
findings.handbook_quote: Monthly tuition is $1,980 for infants and $1,450 for preschoolers, billed monthly and due on the 1st.

findings.requirement: Each licensee must have a written disaster and mass casualty plan readily available.
findings.quote: Each licensee shall have a disaster and mass casualty plan of action. The plan shall be in writing and shall be readily available.
findings.handbook_quote: Our written disaster and mass casualty plan is kept at the front desk.

findings.requirement: Disaster drills must be conducted at least every six months and documented for at least one year.
findings.quote: Disaster drills shall be conducted at least every six months.
findings.handbook_quote: We practice a disaster drill at least every six months and keep a written record of each drill for at least one year.

findings.requirement: Deaths, injuries requiring medical treatment, unusual incidents, suspected abuse, epidemics, poisonings, catastrophes, fires, or explosions must be reported to the Department and parents.
findings.quote: Upon the occurrence during the operation of the child care center of any of the events specified in (d)(1) below, a report shall be made to the Department
findings.handbook_quote: We report to Community Care Licensing, and also to you, any death, injury needing medical treatment, unusual incident, suspected abuse, epidemic outbreak, poisoning, catastrophe, or fire on the premises.
findings.explanation: The handbook's report list leaves out explosions and child absences that threaten a child's health or safety.
findings.fix: We also report to Community Care Licensing any explosion on the premises and any child absence that threatens a child's health or safety.

findings.requirement: The events reported to the Department must also be reported to the child's authorized representative.
findings.quote: The items specified in (d)(1)(A) through (H) above shall also be reported to the child's authorized representative.
findings.handbook_quote: We report to Community Care Licensing, and also to you, any death, injury needing medical treatment, unusual incident, suspected abuse, epidemic outbreak, poisoning, catastrophe, or fire on the premises.

findings.requirement: There must be one teacher visually observing and supervising no more than 12 children, with limited aide exceptions.
findings.quote: There shall be a ratio of one teacher visually observing and supervising no more than 12 children in attendance
findings.handbook_quote: A teacher working without an aide never supervises more than 12 preschool children, and teachers always keep children in sight.

findings.requirement: A teacher and aide may supervise up to 15 children, or 18 preschool children when the aide meets specified qualifications.
findings.quote: The licensee may use teacher aides in a teacher-child ratio of one teacher and one aide for every 15 children in attendance.
findings.handbook_quote: Redwood | 4 to 5 years | 1 fully qualified teacher and 1 aide with at least 6 early childhood units for 18 children | up to 18

findings.requirement: The center must have written admission policies available to the public that match the license limitations.
findings.quote: Every child care center shall have all admission policies in writing and available to the public.
findings.handbook_quote: These policies are available to anyone who asks and match the limits on our license.

findings.requirement: Written admission criteria must designate which children's needs the center can meet.
findings.quote: Written admission criteria designating those children whose needs can be met by the center's program and services.
findings.handbook_quote: We admit children whose needs can be met by our program and services.

findings.requirement: Admission policies must state the ages of children accepted.
findings.quote: The ages of children who will be accepted.
findings.handbook_quote: We accept infants from 6 weeks through 23 months and preschool children from 2 years until they start kindergarten.

findings.requirement: Admission procedures must include personal interviews with the parent or authorized representative.
findings.quote: Conduct one or more personal interviews with the child's parent or authorized representative
findings.handbook_quote: Enrollment begins with a personal interview with the director.

findings.requirement: Parents must receive information about policies, activities, services, regulations, hours, fees, illness procedures, and inspections.
findings.quote: Provides the child's parent or authorized representative with information about the child care center
findings.handbook_quote: we go over our policies, activities, services, licensing regulations, hours, fees, what happens if your child becomes ill or injured, and our daily health check.

findings.requirement: At acceptance, the licensee must inform parents of their rights, including inspection, complaint, and file review rights.
findings.quote: At the time of acceptance of each child in care, the licensee shall inform each child's parent or authorized representative of his/her rights
findings.handbook_quote: When your child is accepted, we give you the Notification of Parents' Rights (LIC 995) and the Caregiver Background Check Process form (LIC 995E).

findings.requirement: Parents have the right to enter and inspect the center without advance notice during normal operating hours.
findings.quote: To enter and inspect the child care center in accordance with Health and Safety Code Section 1596.857.
findings.handbook_quote: Enter and inspect the center without advance notice whenever we are open.

findings.requirement: Parents must be informed of their right to file a complaint with the local licensing office.
findings.quote: To file a complaint against the licensee with the local licensing office in accordance with Health and Safety Code Section 1596.853.
findings.handbook_quote: File a complaint with the local licensing office, and complain or inspect without any discrimination or retaliation.

findings.requirement: The PUB 393 parents' rights poster must be posted in a prominent, publicly accessible area.
findings.quote: The licensee shall post the PUB 393 (8/02), Child Care Center Notification of Parents' Rights Poster in a prominent, publicly accessible area
findings.handbook_quote: The Parents' Rights poster (PUB 393) is posted by our front door.

findings.requirement: The licensee must provide parents the LIC 995E Caregiver Background Check Process form.
findings.quote: The licensee shall provide to the parent or authorized representative the LIC 995E (8/02), Caregiver Background Check Process form.
findings.handbook_quote: we give you the Notification of Parents' Rights (LIC 995) and the Caregiver Background Check Process form (LIC 995E).

findings.requirement: Parents must be able to receive the name, address, and telephone number of the local licensing office upon request.
findings.quote: To receive from the licensee upon request the name, address and telephone number of the local licensing office
findings.handbook_quote: Receive from us, upon request, the name, address, and telephone number of the local licensing office.

findings.requirement: Parents must be informed of any adult granted a criminal record exemption and their association to the center.
findings.quote: To be informed by the licensee, upon request, of the name and type of association to the child care center for any adult who has been granted a criminal record exemption
findings.handbook_quote: Be told, upon request, the name and role of any adult at our center who has been granted a criminal record exemption.

findings.requirement: Parents must receive the LIC 995 Notification of Parents' Rights and LIC 995E, with signed acknowledgement kept in the child's file.
findings.quote: the licensee shall give each parent or authorized representative a copy of the Notification of Parents' Rights (LIC 995 [8/02]) and the LIC 995E
findings.handbook_quote: We ask you to sign the receipt at the bottom of the LIC 995, which we keep in your child's file.

findings.requirement: A current individual written admission agreement must be completed and maintained for each child.
findings.quote: The licensee and the child's authorized representative shall jointly complete a current individual written admission agreement for the child.
findings.handbook_quote: You and the director complete a written admission agreement together.

findings.requirement: Admission agreements must specify basic services, optional services, payment terms, modification conditions, refunds, Department rights, and termination conditions.
findings.quote: Admission agreements shall specify the following: (1) Basic services. (2) Available optional services. (3) Payment provisions
findings.handbook_quote: It lists our basic services, optional services and their rates, your basic rate, who pays, the due date and how often payments are made, how the agreement may be changed, refund conditions, the right of Community Care Licensing to inspect our center and records, and the conditions under which the agreement may be ended.

findings.requirement: The admission agreement must be signed and dated no later than seven calendar days after admission.
findings.quote: The licensee, or his/her designee, and the child's authorized representative shall sign and date the child's admission agreement no later than seven calendar days following admission.
findings.handbook_quote: We both sign and date it no later than seven calendar days after your child starts, and you receive a copy.

findings.requirement: A written medical assessment must be obtained prior to or within 30 days of enrollment.
findings.quote: Prior to, or within 30 calendar days following the enrollment of a child, the licensee shall obtain a written medical assessment of the child.
findings.handbook_quote: Before your child starts, or within 30 calendar days, we need a written medical assessment by or under the supervision of a licensed physician, no more than one year old.

findings.requirement: Admission agreements must state the conditions under which the agreement may be terminated.
findings.quote: Conditions under which the agreement may be terminated.
findings.handbook_quote: Either of us may end the admission agreement with two weeks' written notice.

findings.requirement: An admission agreement is automatically terminated by the death of the child, with no liability after that date.
findings.quote: The admission agreement shall be automatically terminated by the death of the child.

findings.requirement: Children must be immunized against required diseases before admission, unless exempted.
findings.quote: Prior to admission to a child care center, children shall be immunized against diseases as required by the California Code of Regulations, Title 17
findings.handbook_quote: Before admission, children must have the immunizations California requires for their age, or a valid exemption allowed by law.

findings.requirement: The licensee must document each child's immunizations and maintain the documentation while enrolled.
findings.quote: The licensee shall document each child's immunizations and shall maintain such documentation in the center for as long as the child is enrolled.
findings.handbook_quote: We keep your child's immunization record on file and update it as new doses are due.

findings.requirement: Immunizations are not required to be documented for children also enrolled in a public or private elementary school.
findings.quote: The licensee is not required to document immunizations of children also enrolled in a public or private elementary school.

findings.requirement: All information and records obtained from or regarding children must be kept confidential.
findings.quote: All information and records obtained from or regarding children shall be confidential.
findings.handbook_quote: All information in your child's records is confidential and is shared only as the law allows, such as with Community Care Licensing.

findings.requirement: A signed and dated authorization from the authorized representative is required for each activity away from the center.
findings.quote: Signed and dated authorization from the child's authorized representative for each activity away from the center.
findings.handbook_quote: Before every field trip, we ask you to sign and date a permission form for that specific trip.

findings.requirement: A child's records must be open to inspection by the child's authorized representative.
findings.quote: A child's records shall also be open to inspection by the child's authorized representative.
findings.handbook_quote: You may look at your child's records at any time.

findings.requirement: Children must be free from corporal or unusual punishment, pain, humiliation, intimidation, ridicule, coercion, threat, mental abuse, and punitive actions.
findings.quote: To be free from corporal or unusual punishment, infliction of pain, humiliation, intimidation, ridicule, coercion, threat, mental abuse
findings.handbook_quote: We never use spanking or any physical punishment, and never humiliate, threaten, frighten, or ridicule a child. We never take away food, rest, or toileting as a consequence.
findings.explanation: The handbook's discipline list leaves out coercion, mental abuse, and withholding shelter, clothing, medication, or aids to physical functioning.
findings.fix: We also never coerce or mentally abuse a child, and we never withhold shelter, clothing, medication, or aids a child needs.

findings.requirement: Children must not be locked in any room, building, or center premises.
findings.quote: Not to be locked in any room, building or center premises by day or night.
findings.handbook_quote: Children are never locked in any room or area, and we never place a child in any restraining device.

findings.requirement: The center must inform each child's authorized representative of the child's personal rights.
findings.quote: The center shall inform each child's authorized representative of the rights specified in (a) (1) through (8) above.
findings.handbook_quote: We give you a copy of the Personal Rights form (LIC 613A) and ask you to sign the acknowledgment, which we keep in your child's file.

findings.requirement: Parents must receive the LIC 613A Personal Rights form and sign an acknowledgement of receipt.
findings.quote: The center shall give each authorized representative a copy of the Personal Rights form (LIC 613A [9/96]).
findings.handbook_quote: We give you a copy of the Personal Rights form (LIC 613A) and ask you to sign the acknowledgment, which we keep in your child's file.

findings.requirement: A copy of the LIC 613A Personal Rights form must be posted in a prominent, publicly accessible area.
findings.quote: The center shall post a copy of the LIC 613A (9/96) in a prominent, publicly accessible area in the center.
findings.handbook_quote: The form is also posted in our lobby.

findings.requirement: Children must not be placed in any restraining device; only approved postural supports may be used.
findings.quote: Not to be placed in any restraining device. Postural supports may be used as specified in Section 101223.1.
findings.handbook_quote: we never place a child in any restraining device.

findings.requirement: No discipline or punishment that violates a child's personal rights is permitted, even with parent consent.
findings.quote: Any form of discipline or punishment that violates a child's personal rights as specified in Section 101223 shall not be permitted
findings.handbook_quote: None of these practices is allowed even if a parent requests it.

findings.requirement: All vehicle occupants must be secured in an appropriate restraint system, and children must not be left in parked vehicles.
findings.quote: All vehicle occupants shall be secured in an appropriate restraint system.
findings.handbook_quote: Children are never left in a parked vehicle, even for a moment.

findings.requirement: Signs at the entrance must provide the local health department phone number and child passenger restraint information.
findings.quote: The licensee shall post signs at the entrance to the child care center that provide the telephone number of the local health department
findings.handbook_quote: As required by law, signs at our entrance give the local health department's phone number and information about California's child passenger safety seat law.

findings.requirement: Parents must be immediately notified if a child becomes ill or sustains an injury more serious than a minor cut or scratch.
findings.quote: The licensee shall immediately notify the child's authorized representative if the child becomes ill or sustains an injury more serious than a minor cut or scratch.
findings.handbook_quote: We call you immediately for any illness or any injury more serious than a minor cut or scratch.

findings.requirement: Less serious injuries must be documented in the child's record and parents notified when the child is picked up.
findings.quote: the licensee shall document the injury in the child's record and notify the child's authorized representative of the nature of the injury when the child is picked up
findings.handbook_quote: Minor scrapes and bites are cleaned, noted in your child's record, and explained to you at pickup.

findings.requirement: The licensee must obtain emergency medical treatment without specific parent instructions when the parent cannot be reached or delay would be harmful.
findings.quote: The licensee shall obtain emergency medical treatment without specific instructions from the child's authorized representative if the authorized representative cannot be reached immediately
findings.handbook_quote: If we cannot reach you, or if waiting would be dangerous, we will get emergency medical treatment for your child right away.

findings.requirement: Prescription and nonprescription medications require written approval and instructions from the authorized representative.
findings.quote: For each prescription medication, the licensee shall obtain, in writing, approval and instructions from the child's authorized representative
findings.handbook_quote: We give prescription and over-the-counter medicine only with your written approval and instructions for each medicine, matching the label.

findings.requirement: Medications must be centrally stored in a safe place inaccessible to children, with unaltered labels.
findings.quote: All prescription and nonprescription medications shall be centrally stored in accordance with the requirements specified below
findings.handbook_quote: All medicine is stored centrally in a locked cabinet or medicine refrigerator.

findings.requirement: Children with obvious symptoms of illness, including fever or vomiting, must not be accepted.
findings.quote: The licensee shall be responsible for ensuring that children with obvious symptoms of illness including, but not limited to, fever or vomiting, are not accepted.
findings.handbook_quote: Children with obvious signs of illness, such as fever or vomiting, cannot be accepted.

findings.requirement: The center must have a written plan to record medication administration and inform parents daily when medications are given.
findings.quote: The licensee shall develop and implement a written plan to record the administration of prescription and nonprescription medications
findings.handbook_quote: We record every dose and tell you each day when medicine was given.

findings.requirement: Menus must be posted at least one week in advance and copies kept on file for at least 30 days.
findings.quote: Menus shall be in writing and shall be posted at least one week in advance in an area accessible for review
findings.handbook_quote: Weekly menus are posted on the family board at least one week in advance, and we keep dated copies of menus as served for at least 30 days.

findings.requirement: A child must not be served any food to which the child's record indicates an allergy.
findings.quote: A child shall not be served any food to which the child's record indicates he/she has an allergy.
findings.handbook_quote: we never serve a child any food listed as an allergy in their record.

findings.requirement: Modified diets prescribed by a physician as a medical necessity must be provided.
findings.quote: Modified diets prescribed by a child's physician as a medical necessity shall be provided.
findings.handbook_quote: We provide modified diets prescribed by your child's physician as a medical necessity, following the doctor's or dietitian's instructions

findings.requirement: The center must have a written sign-in and sign-out procedure requiring full legal signatures and times.
findings.quote: the licensee shall develop, maintain and implement a written procedure to sign the child in/out of the child care center
findings.handbook_quote: After your child is accepted, sign in on the clipboard by the door using your full legal signature and the time.

findings.requirement: The person who brings the child to and removes the child from the center must sign the child in and out.
findings.quote: The person who brings the child to, and removes the child from, the center shall sign the child in/out.
findings.handbook_quote: We release children only to adults you have listed in writing and will ask for photo ID.

findings.requirement: During nap periods, one teacher may supervise 24 napping children if remaining required teachers are immediately available.
findings.quote: A teacher-child ratio of one teacher supervising 24 napping children is permitted provided that the remaining teachers necessary
findings.handbook_quote: During nap time, one teacher may watch up to 24 napping preschoolers as long as the other teachers needed for ratio are in the building and immediately available.

findings.requirement: Smoking is prohibited on the premises of the child care center.
findings.quote: Smoking is prohibited on the premises of a child care center
findings.handbook_quote: Smoking is not allowed anywhere on our premises at any time.

findings.requirement: Pools and similar bodies of water must be made inaccessible through a pool cover or surrounding fence meeting specified requirements.
findings.quote: All licensees shall ensure the inaccessibility of pools, including swimming pools (in-ground and above-ground), fixed-in-place wading pools, hot tubs, spas, fish ponds
findings.handbook_quote: We have no swimming pool or pond, and children never swim while in our care.

findings.requirement: There must be at least 75 square feet of outdoor activity space per child based on total licensed capacity.
findings.quote: There shall be at least 75 square feet per child of outdoor activity space based on the total licensed capacity.
findings.handbook_quote: We provide at least 35 square feet of indoor and 75 square feet of outdoor play space for every child on our license

findings.requirement: There must be at least 35 square feet of indoor activity space per child based on total licensed capacity.
findings.quote: There shall be at least 35 square feet of indoor activity space per child based on the total licensed capacity.
findings.handbook_quote: We provide at least 35 square feet of indoor and 75 square feet of outdoor play space for every child on our license

findings.requirement: There must be one toilet and one handwashing fixture for every 15 children or fraction thereof.
findings.quote: Based on the total licensed capacity, one toilet and one handwashing fixture shall be maintained for every 15 children or fraction thereof.
findings.handbook_quote: one toilet and sink for every 15 children.

findings.requirement: Hot water delivered to plumbing fixtures used by children must be between 105 and 120 degrees Fahrenheit.
findings.quote: Hot water temperature controls shall be maintained to automatically regulate temperature of hot water delivered to plumbing fixtures used by children
findings.handbook_quote: Hot water at children's sinks stays between 105 and 120 degrees.

findings.requirement: Baby walkers must not be kept or used on the premises of a child care center.
findings.quote: A baby walker shall not be allowed on the premises of a child care center
findings.handbook_quote: Infant room floors are cleaned and disinfected daily, and we do not use baby walkers.

findings.requirement: Potable drinking water must be readily available both indoors and in the outdoor activity area.
findings.quote: Drinking water from a noncontaminating fixture or container shall be readily available both indoors and in the outdoor activity area.
findings.handbook_quote: Drinking water is available indoors and outdoors all day.

findings.requirement: Napping equipment must be arranged so each child has access to a walkway without walking over other children's cots or mats.
findings.quote: Napping equipment shall be arranged so that each child has access to a walkway without having to walk on or over the cots or mats of other children.
findings.handbook_quote: Each child under five has a cot and a space to rest without disturbance, with a clear walkway to every cot.

findings.requirement: There must be one teacher for every four infants in attendance, with limited aide substitution.
findings.quote: There shall be a ratio of one teacher for every four infants in attendance.
findings.handbook_quote: Hummingbird | 6 weeks to 23 months | 1 teacher for every 4 infants | up to 12

findings.requirement: Infant water activities require one adult to two infants near pools or natural bodies of water.
findings.quote: A ratio of one adult to two infants shall be maintained during activities in or near any body of water

findings.requirement: An infant needs and services plan must be completed before the infant's first day, with parent participation and signature.
findings.quote: Prior to the infant's first day at the center, the infant care center director or assistant director shall complete a needs and services plan for the infant.
findings.handbook_quote: Before your baby's first day, the director meets with you to write an infant needs and services plan, which you sign.
findings.explanation: The handbook's infant needs and services plan does not mention a toilet-training plan when one applies.
findings.fix: Before your baby's first day, the director meets with you to write an infant needs and services plan, which you sign. It includes your baby's feeding plan, the Individual Infant Sleeping Plan (LIC 9227), which you sign and date, a toilet-training plan if your baby is being toilet trained, any special services your baby needs, and a schedule for future meetings. We update it with you at least every three months.

findings.requirement: Infants must not be confined to cribs, high chairs, playpens, or similar equipment as discipline or punishment.
findings.quote: Confinement to cribs, high chairs, playpens or other similar furniture or equipment shall not be permitted as a form of discipline
findings.handbook_quote: Infants are never kept in a crib, high chair, or playpen as a punishment.

findings.requirement: Infants transported in motor vehicles must be secured in an infant car seat according to manufacturer's instructions.
findings.quote: When transporting infants in any motor vehicle, the licensee shall secure each infant in a child passenger restraint system, i.e., a car seat designed for an infant.
findings.handbook_quote: secure every passenger in a seat belt or car seat, with infants in rear-facing infant car seats installed according to the manufacturer's instructions.

findings.requirement: Motor vehicles used to transport infants must contain a first-aid kit with at least the supplies specified in Section 101226(d).
findings.quote: Motor vehicles used to transport infants shall contain a first-aid kit containing at least the supplies specified in Section 101226(d).
findings.handbook_quote: Ratios are kept in the van, and a first aid kit rides along.
findings.explanation: The handbook mentions a first-aid kit but does not state that it contains at least the required supplies.
findings.fix: Our vans carry a first-aid kit with at least a first-aid manual, sterile dressings, bandages, adhesive tape, scissors, tweezers, a thermometer, and antiseptic solution.

findings.requirement: Staff-infant ratios must be maintained while transporting infants, whether the vehicle is moving or parked.
findings.quote: The staff-infant ratio shall be maintained while transporting infants in motor vehicles.
findings.handbook_quote: Ratios are kept in the van, and a first aid kit rides along.

findings.requirement: Infants in motor vehicles must have constant adult supervision and must not be left unattended under any circumstances.
findings.quote: Infants in motor vehicles shall have constant adult supervision and shall not be left unattended under any circumstances.
findings.handbook_quote: Children are never left in a parked vehicle, even for a moment.

findings.requirement: Each infant must have an individual feeding plan completed and available before the first day.
findings.quote: There shall be an individual feeding plan for each infant.
findings.handbook_quote: Each baby has an individual feeding plan, written with you before the first day, covering schedule, breast milk or formula brand, new foods, textures, and allergies.
findings.explanation: The handbook's feeding plan description leaves out several items the rule requires, such as physician instructions, food likes and dislikes, and cup and utensil introduction.
findings.fix: Each baby has an individual feeding plan, written with you before the first day. It includes any instructions from your baby's physician, feeding schedule, breast milk or formula, plans for new foods and textures, food likes and dislikes, allergies, and when to introduce cups and utensils.

findings.requirement: Bottles must not be propped for infants, and infants must not carry bottles while ambulatory.
findings.quote: At no time shall a bottle be propped for an infant. An infant shall not be allowed to carry a bottle while ambulatory.
findings.handbook_quote: Babies are always held for bottle feeding, bottles are never propped, and walking babies do not carry bottles.

findings.requirement: Infant care centers must not serve honey or corn syrup to any infant.
findings.quote: The infant care center shall not serve honey or corn syrup to any infant.
findings.handbook_quote: Babies are always held for bottle feeding, bottles are never propped, and walking babies do not carry bottles. We never serve honey or corn syrup.

findings.requirement: Infants being toilet trained must have a written toilet-training plan developed with the parent.
findings.quote: There shall be a written toilet-training plan for infants being toilet trained.
findings.handbook_quote: When your toddler is ready, we write a toilet-training plan with you covering methods, potty equipment, and clothing.

findings.requirement: Infants must be diapered on a changing table or approved floor pad, and changing surfaces must be disinfected after each use.
findings.quote: Each infant shall be diapered on a changing table.
findings.handbook_quote: Babies are diapered on a changing table that is disinfected after every change, and babies are never left alone on it.

findings.requirement: Sleeping infants must be directly observed by sight and sound, with physical checks every 15 minutes documented.
findings.quote: Sleeping infants shall be directly observed by sight and sound at all times.
findings.handbook_quote: A teacher watches and listens to sleeping babies at all times and physically checks each sleeping baby every 15 minutes, writing down the time and their initials on the sleep log.
findings.explanation: The handbook's sleep-check documentation does not mention recording the date and the infant's name.
findings.fix: A teacher watches and listens to sleeping babies at all times and physically checks each sleeping baby every 15 minutes, writing down the date, the baby's name, the time, and the staff member's initials on the sleep log.

findings.requirement: Each infant must be constantly supervised and under direct visual observation by a staff person at all times.
findings.quote: Each infant shall be constantly supervised and under direct visual observation and supervision by a staff person at all times.
findings.handbook_quote: Every baby is in a teacher's direct view at all times.

findings.requirement: Infants up to 12 months must be placed on their backs for sleeping unless a written medical exemption applies.
findings.quote: Staff shall place infants up to 12 months of age on their backs for sleeping.
findings.handbook_quote: Babies under 12 months are always placed on their backs to sleep unless a physician has signed a medical exemption.
findings.explanation: The handbook does not describe the required contents of a written medical exemption for an alternative sleep position.
findings.fix: Babies under 12 months are always placed on their backs to sleep unless a licensed physician has provided a written medical exemption with instructions, duration, contact information, and signature, which we keep in your baby's file.

findings.requirement: An infant must not be swaddled while in care.
findings.quote: An infant shall not be swaddled while in care.
findings.handbook_quote: We never swaddle and never cover a baby's head.

findings.requirement: An infant's head must not be covered while sleeping.
findings.quote: An infant's head shall not be covered while sleeping.
findings.handbook_quote: We never swaddle and never cover a baby's head.

findings.requirement: Caregivers must wash hands with soap and water before each feeding and after each diaper change.
findings.quote: Each caregiver shall wash his/her hands with soap and water before each feeding and after each diaper change.
findings.handbook_quote: Teachers wash their hands with soap and water before every feeding and after every diaper change.

findings.requirement: Infant care areas must follow specified washing, cleaning, and sanitizing requirements, including daily floor cleaning and disinfecting.
findings.quote: Washing, cleaning and sanitizing requirements for areas used by staff with infants, or for areas that infants have access to, are as follows
findings.handbook_quote: Infant room floors are cleaned and disinfected daily, and we do not use baby walkers.
findings.explanation: The handbook mentions daily floor cleaning but leaves out other required cleaning, sanitizing, and disinfecting practices.
findings.fix: We clean and disinfect infant areas following our daily and weekly routines, including floors, walls, diaper-changing surfaces, sinks, mouthed toys, and linens, and we prepare our disinfecting solution fresh each day.

findings.requirement: Infants unable to climb out of a crib must be provided a crib meeting consumer product safety standards, with a firm fitted mattress.
findings.quote: A crib or portable crib meeting United States Consumer Product Safety Commission safety standards shall be provided for each infant who is unable to climb out of a crib.
findings.handbook_quote: Babies sleep in their own safety-approved crib with a firm, fitted mattress and nothing else inside except a pacifier with nothing attached

findings.requirement: Bumper pads must not be used in infant cribs.
findings.quote: Bumper pads shall not be used.
findings.handbook_quote: no blankets, pillows, toys, or bumper pads.

findings.requirement: Infant cribs must be free from all loose articles and objects, including blankets and pillows.
findings.quote: Cribs shall be free from all loose articles and objects, including blankets and pillows.
findings.handbook_quote: with a firm, fitted mattress and nothing else inside except a pacifier with nothing attached: no blankets, pillows, toys, or bumper pads.

findings.requirement: School-age programs must have one teacher and one aide for every 28 children, with one teacher supervising no more than 14.
findings.quote: There shall be a staffing ratio of one teacher and one aide present to every 28 children in attendance.

findings.requirement: Medical assessments are not required for school-age children enrolled in a public or private school.
findings.quote: The licensee is not required to document medical assessments on school-age children who are enrolled in a public or private school.

findings.requirement: School-age children may leave on their own only with a written agreement signed by the director and authorized representative.
findings.quote: Center staff shall sign out a school-age child whose authorized representative has agreed in writing to allow the child to leave the center on his/her own.

findings.requirement: Before- and after-school programs must make available and offer nutritious snacks to children.
findings.quote: Center programs providing before- and/or after-school care shall make available and offer nutritious snacks to children.

findings.requirement: School-age programs meeting Health and Safety Code Section 1596.806 requirements are exempt from outdoor activity space square-footage requirements.
findings.quote: Each school-age child care program and each single license child care center operating with only school-age children that meets the requirements of Health and Safety Code Section 1596.806 is exempt from square-footage requirements

findings.requirement: School-age programs meeting Health and Safety Code Section 1596.806 requirements are exempt from indoor activity space square-footage requirements.
findings.quote: School-age child care programs that meet the requirements of Health and Safety Code Section 1596.806 are exempt from square-footage requirements for indoor activity space.

findings.requirement: School-age programs meeting Health and Safety Code Section 1596.806 requirements are exempt from toilet requirements.
findings.quote: School-age child care programs that meet the requirements of Health and Safety Code Section 1596.806 are exempt from toilet requirements.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill center directors must meet specified education, health and safety training, or licensed health professional qualifications.
findings.quote: The director of a Level I or Level II child care center for mildly ill children shall, prior to employment, meet the requirements of Section 101615(b)(1) OR (2).

findings.requirement: Health consultant qualification evidence must include a photocopy of the license.
findings.quote: A photocopy of the license; and

findings.requirement: Health consultant qualification evidence must include documentation of written or verbal contact with the appropriate licensing board.
findings.quote: Documentation of written or verbal contact with the appropriate State of California licensing board to verify licensure status.

findings.requirement: Health consultant qualification evidence must include both a photocopy of the license and documentation of contact with the licensing board.
findings.quote: A photocopy of the license; and (2) Documentation of written or verbal contact with the appropriate State of California licensing board

findings.requirement: Health consultant qualification evidence must include a photocopy of the license and documentation of contact with the licensing board.

findings.quote: A photocopy of the license; and (2) Documentation of written or verbal contact with the appropriate State of California licensing board to verify licensure status.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill center teachers must complete specified units in childhood illness and early childhood education and health and safety training.
findings.quote: prior to employment a teacher shall complete three postsecondary semester or equivalent quarter units in the identification, transmission, control and care of common childhood illnesses

findings.requirement: Mildly ill center staff and volunteers providing care must complete at least 20 hours of specified training within two weeks of starting.
findings.quote: All staff and volunteers whose duties include the provision of care to, and the supervision and protection of, mildly ill children shall complete training

findings.requirement: Mildly ill programs must maintain specified ratios: one teacher to three infants, six preschool children, or eight school-age children.
findings.quote: There shall be a ratio of one teacher to every three infants in attendance.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill center admission policies must specify the conditions, symptoms, and illnesses for which children will and will not be accepted.
findings.quote: The written admission policies for child care centers for mildly ill children shall specify the conditions/symptoms/illnesses for which children will and will not be accepted

findings.requirement: Water activities in pools, wading pools, or natural bodies of water are not permitted in mildly ill centers.
findings.quote: Water activities in or near any of the following bodies of water shall not be permitted in a child care center for mildly ill children

findings.requirement: A written medical assessment for a mildly ill child must be obtained if a qualified staff person determines it is necessary based on symptoms or illness.
findings.quote: A written medical assessment for the child shall be obtained from the child's authorized representative if a qualified staff person determines that one is necessary

findings.requirement: Mildly ill child records must include medical assessments, notification records, medications, plan of care, daily inspection forms, health clearances, observations, and allergies.
findings.quote: Each child's record shall include: (1) A copy of the written medical assessment, when one has been required

findings.requirement: Mildly ill child records must include a copy of the written medical assessment when required, or a dated notation if not required.
findings.quote: A copy of the written medical assessment, when one has been required, as specified in Section 101620.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill medical assessments must verify the child is not contagious or a health risk and identify special requirements and medications.
findings.quote: The medical assessment shall include: (A) Verification that the child's symptoms or illness does not pose a risk to the child or others at the center.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill medical assessments must verify a recent negative tuberculosis test unless the child is concurrently enrolled in a licensed center or school.
findings.quote: Verification of the child's recent negative test for tuberculosis unless the child is concurrently enrolled in a licensed child care center or a public or private school.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill medical assessments must identify ambulatory status and restrictions on activities.
findings.quote: Ambulatory status and restrictions on activities.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill medical assessments must identify prescription and nonprescription medications the child must take while at the center.
findings.quote: Identification of prescription and nonprescription medications that the child must take while at the center.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill medical assessments must identify the child's special requirements.
findings.quote: Identification of the child's special requirements.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill medical assessments must be filed in the child's record.
findings.quote: Medical assessments shall be filed in the child's record.

findings.requirement: When a medical assessment is not required for a mildly ill child, a dated notation must be made in the child's record.
findings.quote: When a medical assessment is not required, the licensee shall make a dated notation to that effect in the child's record.

findings.requirement: If a mildly ill child's illness worsens beyond the licensed level of care, the parent must be notified and must remove the child.
findings.quote: the licensee shall immediately notify the child's authorized representative and require the child's authorized representative to remove the child from the center.

findings.requirement: Each mildly ill child must have a written plan of care developed with the parent and updated daily.
findings.quote: A written plan of care shall be developed for each child and shall be updated daily.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill child records must include information regarding any allergies the child may have.
findings.quote: Information regarding any allergies the child may have.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill child records must include health clearances when required.
findings.quote: Health clearances, when required, as specified in Section 101626.1(f).

findings.requirement: Mildly ill child records must include information regarding instances of authorized representative notification.
findings.quote: A copy of information regarding instances of authorized representative notification as specified in Sections 101626(b) and (b)(1).

findings.requirement: Mildly ill child records must include a copy of the child's plan of care.
findings.quote: A copy of the child's plan of care as specified in Section 101626(c).

findings.requirement: Mildly ill child records must include observations of the child.
findings.quote: Observations of the child as specified in Section 101626.3(b).

findings.requirement: Mildly ill centers must have continuing health consultation from a licensed physician or registered nurse with pediatric experience.
findings.quote: Every center shall have provisions for continuing health consultation from a physician or registered nurse with a current and active license

findings.requirement: Health consultation must include developing written plans and procedures for admissions, operations, inspections, communicable disease surveillance, and individual child care.
findings.quote: Health consultation shall include developing written plans and procedures and, if necessary, forms for the following, all of which shall be maintained at the center

findings.requirement: Health consultation must include liaison with local health departments.
findings.quote:
Health consultation shall include developing written plans and procedures and, if necessary, forms for the following, all of which shall be maintained at the center:
(A) Admissions criteria, center operating policies and procedures, daily inspection procedures, procedures for the surveillance of communicable diseases, and plans for the care of individual children.
(B) Liaison with local health departments.

findings.requirement: Health consultants must have a current and active license and pediatric experience or training obtained within the last five years.
findings.quote: This health professional shall have pediatric experience/training obtained within the last five years.

findings.requirement: Health consultation may be provided by a staff member who is also a health professional as part of staff duties, or by an outside consultant.
findings.quote: Health consultation may be provided by a staff member who is also a health professional as specified in Section 101626(d), as part of his/her staff duties

findings.requirement: Health consultation for mildly ill centers must occur quarterly or more often, and not less than semiannually, with written reports.
findings.quote: Health consultation shall occur quarterly or more often, if necessary, and not less than semiannually.

findings.requirement: If health consultation is provided by an outside consultant, a written contract or letter of agreement must be maintained in the center's files.
findings.quote: If health consultation is provided by an outside consultant, a written contract or letter of agreement between the consultant and the center shall be prepared.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill centers must maintain each health consultant's name, address, telephone number, area of specialization, and evidence of qualifications.
findings.quote: Each center shall maintain in its files each health consultant's name, address, telephone number, area of specialization and evidence of qualifications.

findings.requirement: Health consultation must include recordkeeping and reporting of accidents and illnesses involving staff and children.
findings.quote: Recordkeeping and reporting of accidents and illnesses involving staff and children.

findings.requirement: Health consultation must include obtaining emergency health care, including listing emergency telephone numbers.
findings.quote: Obtaining emergency health care, including provisions for listing emergency telephone numbers.

findings.requirement: Health consultation must include administration, handling, and storage of medications.
findings.quote: Administration, handling and storage of medications.

findings.requirement: Health consultation must include emergency first-aid procedures and assurance of trained staff availability.
findings.quote: Emergency first-aid procedures and assurance of the availability of staff trained in such procedures.

findings.requirement: Health consultation must include establishment of an isolation area and development of related procedures.
findings.quote: Establishment of an isolation area and development of related procedures.

findings.requirement: Health consultation must include provision of continuing health-care services to children without access, including referrals.
findings.quote: Provision of continuing health-care services to children in attendance who do not already have access to such services

findings.requirement: Health consultation must include provision of staff training as specified in Section 101616.2.
findings.quote: Provision of staff training as specified in Section 101616.2.

findings.requirement: Evidence of a health consultant's qualifications must include a photocopy of the license and documentation of contact with the licensing board.
findings.quote: Evidence of qualifications shall include, but not be limited to, verification of licensure required in Section 101626(d) as demonstrated by the following

findings.requirement: Each mildly ill child must receive a daily inspection for illness by a qualified staff person before acceptance.
findings.quote: Upon arrival each day at the center, each child shall have a daily inspection for illness to determine if the child is appropriate for placement

findings.requirement: Mildly ill centers must maintain the most current edition of a manual on identification and control of communicable diseases.
findings.quote: The licensee shall maintain the most current edition of a manual on the identification and control of communicable diseases.

findings.requirement: A qualified staff person must perform and document the daily inspection for illness for mildly ill children.
findings.quote: A qualified staff person shall perform and document the completion of the daily inspection for illness.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill children's body temperatures must be determined using a thermometer with a disposable plastic probe cover.
findings.quote: a child's body temperature shall be determined by using a thermometer with a disposable plastic (Probe) cover.

findings.requirement: After each health consultation, the consultant must prepare a written report of findings and recommendations, maintained in the center's files.
findings.quote: After each consultation, the consultant shall prepare a written report of his/her findings and recommendations. These reports shall be maintained in the center's files.

findings.requirement: If consultation is not necessary during a quarter, a notation explaining why must be made in the center's files.
findings.quote: If consultation is not necessary during a quarter, a notation explaining why shall be made in the center's files.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill centers must not accept or retain children with specified conditions, symptoms, or illnesses.
findings.quote: the licensee shall not accept or retain for care any child with any of the following conditions/symptoms/illnesses or combination thereof

findings.requirement: The subchapter must not be interpreted to require exclusion of a child with a chronic condition protected under the ADA unless the child also has an excluding condition.
findings.quote: This subchapter shall not be interpreted to require the exclusion of a child with a chronic condition protected under the Americans With Disabilities Act of 1990

findings.requirement: The authorized representative must remain in the center until the daily inspection for illness is completed and the child is accepted.
findings.quote: The licensee shall require the child's authorized representative to remain in the center until the daily inspection for illness is completed and the child is accepted for care.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill centers must develop and implement a written procedure for completing daily inspections for illness, including a documentation form.
findings.quote: The licensee shall develop and implement a written procedure for completing daily inspections for illness, which shall include developing a form to document

findings.requirement: The health consultant must be consulted on the development of the daily inspection procedure and form for mildly ill centers.
findings.quote: As required by Section 101626(d), the health consultant shall be consulted on the development of the procedure and form specified in Section 101626.1(c).

findings.requirement: A mildly ill center may accept a child with specified conditions if a written health clearance states the child is diagnosed, not contagious, and not a health risk.
findings.quote: A Level I or Level II center may accept a child with any of the conditions/symptoms/illnesses as specified in Section 101626.1(e) if the licensee has obtained a written health clearance

findings.requirement: Verbal approval from a physician may be accepted if the written health clearance is obtained within 24 hours.
findings.quote: A licensee may accept a child for care under Section 101626.1(f) upon the verbal approval of a physician or other health professional

findings.requirement: Written health clearances for mildly ill children must be kept in the child's record.
findings.quote: The written health clearance, which shall be kept in the child's record, shall be obtained from a physician or other health professional

findings.requirement: Receipt of verbal approval for a mildly ill child must be recorded immediately in the child's record with specified details.
findings.quote: Receipt of verbal approval as specified in Section 101626.1(f)(2) shall be recorded immediately in the child's record.

findings.requirement: Level II mildly ill centers may accept children with diarrhea due to confirmed shigella, salmonella, or giardia only under specified isolation and approval conditions.
findings.quote: A Level II center may accept a child with diarrhea due to confirmed shigella, salmonella or giardia 24 hours after treatment has been initiated

findings.requirement: Mildly ill centers must not accept or retain children with diarrhea due to campylobacter or cryptosporidium under any circumstances.
findings.quote: The licensee shall not, under any circumstances, accept or retain for care any child with any of the following conditions/symptoms/illnesses: (1) Diarrhea due to campylobacter or cryptosporidium.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill centers must not accept or retain children in contagious stages of measles, rubella, pertussis, diphtheria, or tuberculosis.
findings.quote: Contagious stages of measles, rubella, pertussis, diphtheria or tuberculosis.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill centers must not accept or retain children with untreated infestations such as head lice or scabies.
findings.quote: Untreated infestation (such as head lice, scabies).

findings.requirement: Level II mildly ill centers may accept children in contagious stages of chicken pox or mumps only under specified isolation and approval conditions.
findings.quote: A Level II center may accept a child in the contagious stages of chicken pox or mumps, if prior approval is obtained from the Department

findings.requirement: Mildly ill centers must have an isolation area and isolate children when specified conditions occur.
findings.quote: A center shall be equipped with an isolation area to care for any child as specified in Section 101626.2(c).

findings.requirement: Children in the mildly ill isolation area must be under constant observation by a teacher present in the isolation area.
findings.quote: Children in the isolation area shall be under the constant observation of a teacher who is present in the isolation area itself.

findings.requirement: A child must remain in the mildly ill isolation area only until the authorized representative can remove the child from the center.
findings.quote: A child shall remain in the isolation area only until the child's authorized representative can remove the child from the center

findings.requirement: Changes in a mildly ill child's behavior or worsening illness must be reported to the parent and recorded the same day.
findings.quote: Any changes in the child's behavior or any signs of the child's illness worsening shall be reported to the child's authorized representative and recorded in the child's record on the day they occur.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill children with elevated temperatures must have temperatures taken at specified intervals based on age.
findings.quote: Any child with a body temperature of 100 F (37.8 C) (oral) or 101 F (38.3 C) (rectal or by ear) or 99 F (37.2 C) (axillary), or higher, shall have his/her body temperature taken during the day

findings.requirement: Mildly ill centers must record daily observations of behavior and symptoms when indicated by the nature of the child's illness.
findings.quote: If indicated by the nature of the child's illness at any time when the child is in care, staff shall record daily observations of the child's behavior and symptoms

findings.requirement: Mildly ill children with elevated temperatures must have temperatures taken at specified intervals based on age.
findings.quote: Any child with a body temperature of 100 F (37.8 C) (oral) or 101 F (38.3 C) (rectal or by ear) or 99 F (37.2 C) (axillary), or higher, shall have his/her body temperature taken during the day as follows

findings.requirement: Mildly ill children's meals and snacks must be prepared according to each child's admission agreement and plan of care.
findings.quote: For mildly ill children, individual meals and snacks shall be prepared in accordance with the requirements of each child's admission agreement and plan of care.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill infants' meals and snacks must be prepared according to each infant's admission agreement, feeding plan, and plan of care.
findings.quote: For mildly ill infants, individual meals and snacks shall be prepared in accordance with the requirements of each infant's admission agreement, feeding plan and plan of care.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill children must be signed in and out by their authorized representative.
findings.quote: The licensee shall require that each child be signed in and out by his/her authorized representative.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill centers must use only disposable diapers unless cloth diapers are specified in the child's plan of care.
findings.quote: Only disposable diapers shall be used unless cloth diapers are specified in the infant's or child's plan of care.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill centers must have a written plan for indoor and outdoor activities meeting children's needs.
findings.quote: The licensee shall develop, maintain and implement a written plan to ensure the provision of indoor and outdoor activities designed to meet the needs of mildly ill children.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill children must be given the opportunity to nap or sleep whenever they wish without being disturbed.
findings.quote: Each child, unless it is not appropriate because of the nature of his/her illness, shall be given the opportunity to nap/sleep whenever he/she wishes

findings.requirement: Mildly ill centers must follow specified handwashing, cleaning, and sanitizing procedures, including daily floor cleaning and disinfecting.
findings.quote: Washing, cleaning and sanitizing requirements for areas used by staff and children, or for areas that children have access to, shall include

findings.requirement: Mildly ill indoor activity space must be physically separate from other components, with additional napping space requirements.
findings.quote: indoor activity space for the Level I or Level II component shall be physically separate from indoor activity space for any other child care center component

findings.requirement: Mildly ill centers must provide at least 20 square feet of outdoor activity space per child, physically separate from well children.
findings.quote: There shall be at least 20 square feet of outdoor activity space per child based on the total licensed capacity.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill napping areas must provide at least 15 square feet per child's bed, cot, mat, or couch, in addition to activity space.
findings.quote: In the designated napping area, there shall be at least 15 square feet of indoor space for each child's bed, cot, floor mat or couch

findings.requirement: Beds, cots, mats, couches, blankets, and pillows must be available and accessible for mildly ill children whenever they are present.
findings.quote: Beds, cots, floor mats or couches, as well as blankets and pillows, shall be available and accessible for use by mildly ill children whenever mildly ill children are present.

findings.requirement: Mildly ill infants must not have access to pillows.
findings.quote: Mildly ill infants shall not have access to pillows.

findings.requirement: A mildly ill center's total licensed capacity must not exceed 10 children for every toilet and handwashing sink.
findings.quote: the total licensed capacity of a center shall not exceed 10 mildly ill children for every toilet and handwashing sink.

findings.requirement: Each mildly ill child must use a cup or bottle labeled with their name, or a single-use disposable cup.
findings.quote: Each child shall use a cup or bottle labeled with his/her name, or a single-use disposable cup.

findings.requirement: Infant sleep position exception
findings.quote: Infants with an Individual Infant Sleeping Plan [LIC 9227 (3/20)] that have Section C of the form completed and signed by an authorized representative shall be placed on their back when first laid down to sleep. In the event the infant changes position, the infant may remain in the alternative position.
findings.handbook_quote: Babies under 12 months are always placed on their backs to sleep unless a physician has signed a medical exemption.
findings.explanation: The rule also allows an infant to remain in an alternative sleep position when Section C of the Individual Infant Sleeping Plan is completed and signed by an authorized representative.
findings.fix: Babies under 12 months are placed on their backs to sleep. If an infant rolls to another position and Section C of the Individual Infant Sleeping Plan (LIC 9227) is completed and signed by the authorized representative, the infant may remain in that position; a physician's written exemption is also followed.

findings.requirement: Infant sleep check documentation
findings.quote: Staff shall physically check on sleeping infants every 15 minutes and document the following: 1. Labored breathing. 2. Signs of distress, which includes but is not limited to flushed skin color, increase in body temperature, and restlessness. 3. Infants up to 12 months of age who are sleeping in a position other than on their back.
findings.handbook_quote: A teacher watches and listens to sleeping babies at all times and physically checks each sleeping baby every 15 minutes, writing down the time and their initials on the sleep log.
findings.explanation: The rule requires the 15-minute check to document labored breathing, signs of distress, and sleep position, not only the time and initials.
findings.fix: We physically check each sleeping baby every 15 minutes and record the time, staff initials, and any labored breathing, signs of distress, or non-back sleep position.
